computer.text: In 1936, what did the word “computer” mean?

electronic.text: An electronic machine that does sums
electronic.why: Electronic computers came later. In 1936, a computer was a person.

person.text: A person who calculates by hand
person.why: Turing built his machine from a picture of such a person at work.

tables.why: People used such books, but the word “computer” meant the person who calculates.

tape.text: Which part of the human computer's work became the tape?

pencil.why: The pencil writes in one square at a time. It is closer to the head, which reads and writes one cell.

mind.why: The state of mind became the machine's state, not the tape.

paper.why: Turing kept one long row of squares, and that row became the tape.

state.text: What does the machine's state hold?

memory.text: What the machine must remember about its work so far
memory.why: Like a state of mind, the state holds things such as “I carry a 1”.

cell.text: The symbol in the cell under the head
cell.why: The head reads that symbol. The state is a separate thing, and together they pick the rule.

whole-tape.why: The machine sees only one cell at a time. The tape holds the symbols, not the state.

rules.why: The rules stay the same for the whole run. The state changes from step to step.

first-machine.text: When does Turing's first machine stop?

four-steps.text: After four steps, when each state has run once
four-steps.why: After 𝔨, the machine goes back to 𝔟 and goes on.

end-of-tape.text: When it reaches the end of the tape
end-of-tape.why: The tape has no end, so the machine never runs out of cells.

never.why: Every rule leads to another state, so the machine prints 0 1 0 1 … forever.

carry.text: Binary plus one is in state q1 and reads a 1. What does it do?

write-one-stop.why: That is what happens with a 0 or a blank. A 1 means there is a carry.

write-zero-left.why: 1 plus 1 makes 0 with a carry, so the machine moves left to add the carry there.

move-right.text: It moves right to find the end of the number
move-right.why: That is what state q0 does. In q1, the machine moves left.
